note: Modes are compatible and stack. Each mode adds mandatory directives and forces a specific deck to be drawn. Stacking more than three modes tends to produce noise rather than strangeness - the draw script warns above three.

modes.label: Infant mode - unlearn function, name, and causality
directives: Ignore the official function of every object involved; treat what it does when misused as what it is for.
Let similar-sounding names imply real kinship between unrelated things, and follow that kinship seriously.
Invert the order of cause and effect at least once and keep the inversion consistent.
Do not maintain the boundaries alive/dead, inside/outside, self/other, real/imagined unless the world's own new law restores them.
Ask 'why must it be so?' of every premise that no one usually states.
modes.guard: Infant logic, adult execution. Childlike results (cute, silly, whimsical for its own sake) are a failure of this mode, not an expression of it.

modes.label: Non-anthropocentric mode - remove human usefulness
directives: Nothing here exists for human benefit, and nothing was designed with a human in mind.
Humans, if present, are weather, terrain, or an accident - never the audience.
If the result would be a product, a tool, or a service, it is disqualified in this mode.
Do not give it a humanoid body plan, a face, or motives that map onto human wants.
modes.guard: Check every sentence containing 'so that' or 'in order to'. If the beneficiary is a person, rewrite.

modes.label: Rule-break mode - change physics, time, or selfhood rather than appearance
directives: Delete or invert at least one law of the drawn constraint deck and never restore it quietly.
Install a replacement law that makes something newly impossible; state that impossibility explicitly.
Derive at least three consequences from the new law that you did not intend when you wrote it.
The visual appearance may be perfectly mundane. The strangeness lives in what is possible, not in what is seen.
modes.guard: If deleting the visual description leaves the idea intact, the mode was applied. If it leaves nothing, it was not.

modes.label: Sense and feeling mode - invent a perception or an unnamed emotion
directives: Invent at least one sense or one affect that has no existing name, and answer all four required fields for it.
Show one ordinary daily situation reorganized by it - a greeting, a queue, a meal, a goodbye.
Name the new injustice, misunderstanding, or grief it creates.
Do not translate the new sense into sight or sound as a shortcut, and do not render feelings as colors.
modes.guard: A sense that only adds convenience is a feature. A sense that adds a new way to be wronged is an invention.

modes.label: Extremal mode - discard everything safe
directives: Discard every candidate that any competent writer would reach within one minute of hearing the prompt.
Raise all rubric thresholds: mean 9.0, no axis below 8.
Draw twice as many domains and hybridize from the three most distant survivors.
If nothing survives, report that honestly and show the closest failure with the reason it failed.
modes.guard: Extremal is not louder. It is a stricter cull with the same coherence requirement.

modes.label: Grounded mode - keep the alien principle, add one operational path
directives: Keep the broken law and the new law intact. Do not soften the premise to make it buildable.
Add exactly one section describing how a person could actually encounter, use, or make a version of this within current constraints.
State plainly which part of the principle does not survive that translation.
Never let the operational path retro-edit the principle into something ordinary.
modes.guard: Use with anchor 2 or 3 when the user needs the result for a real product, story, or brief.

anchors.label: Unbound
anchors.rule: No requirement of buildability, usefulness, or human relevance. Internal consistency is the only obligation.

anchors.label: Legible
anchors.rule: Must be describable to a non-expert in three sentences without analogy to a known work.

anchors.label: Stageable
anchors.rule: Must be renderable as a concrete scene, artifact, or scenario a team could produce or film.

anchors.label: Operable
anchors.rule: Must include one path to a real prototype, publication, or product, with the loss from that translation stated.
